json_result.metric: exact FP16 bit-pattern comparison vs once-rounded real sigmoid (CPU FP64 reference)

evidence.summary: Exhaustive comparison over all 63488 finite FP16 encodings found 7 exact bit-pattern mismatches between kernel output and the once-rounded sigmoid (one-ULP errors near 0.5 for |x|<0.011). High-precision Decimal recomputation (t8) confirms the exact sigmoid value lies strictly on the reference's side of the FP16 midpoint in all 7 cases, so these are genuine correct-rounding violations, not reference artifacts. E.g. x=0.0029296875: exact sigmoid 0.5007324213511315 < midpoint 0.500732421875, correct FP16 code 14337, kernel produced 14338. x=-0.00146484375: exact 0.4996337891279836 > midpoint 0.4996337890625, correct code 14335, kernel produced 14334.

rationale: The kernel computes sigmoid via exp(-|x|) in fp32 with div_rn and a single cvt.rn.f16.f32; intermediate fp32 rounding of exp and the division could push some values to a different FP16 code than the correctly rounded real sigmoid value.

scope_evidence.summary: Each output must be that value rounded ONCE to IEEE binary16 round-to-nearest-even; every finite FP16 encoding is legal; one failing legal input is evidence against the implementation.

scope_rationale: Contract requires exact FP16 bit patterns equal to the once-rounded real sigmoid over the whole legal finite FP16 input domain.
statement: The kernel's final FP16 output differs from the once-rounded real sigmoid for at least one legal finite FP16 input.
